analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, head lines 729-739. It adds prose to the 'Focused Tooling Checks' section about the PR-reviewer tooling tests: batch segmentation of large fixtures, a 500-request stop, a larger output default, client timeouts, stage-admission failure identification, manual GitHub job reruns doing no paid work, bounded runtime configuration, and human review for incomplete outcomes. It also states that manual dispatch is restricted to unpaid preflight and that the scanner deadline stays below the job timeout. There are no code, workflow, protocol or crypto changes in the supplied evidence. Nothing here touches the provider-facing threat model: the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002), provider key custody (A-003), App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the fan helper (TB-010), or the attestation chain (TB-009). I reviewed the rest of the file's base text (the Provider Endpoint Resumption and Logout section, the SSD test working volume section, the cache test commands and the env -i recipes) as surrounding context. The unchanged parts describe isolated tests, synthetic credentials and never pointing tests at production, and the diff does not weaken those. The new text describes the reviewer tooling's cost controls and fail-closed behavior, which are positive or neutral. The documented behaviors (workflow dispatch restriction, deadline below job timeout, no paid work on rerun) are implemented in files not supplied, so this PR cannot establish that they hold. That is an unverified contract and a documentation-accuracy question, not a regression. No findings, and no threat-model update is needed.
